text.arabic_uthmani: وَإِذَا حُشِرَ ٱلنَّاسُ كَانُوا۟ لَهُمْ أَعْدَآءًۭ وَكَانُوا۟ بِعِبَادَتِهِمْ كَٰفِرِينَ

words.root_display: not applicable; particle with no lexical root
words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction carrying the prior false-worship scene into a judgment-time frame
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) does more than add another sentence. It carries the unanswered invocation of 46:5 forward and immediately hands it to the certain-time frame that follows. The tiny connector therefore makes the judgment scene sound continuous with the prior false-worship argument, while still creating an audible turn into the gathering.

topics.headline: resumptive judgment turn
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 46:6 is not detached from 46:5; the prior invocation-futility is carried into the gathering scene.
topics.reason: The local clause evidence licenses a temporal opening after the connector, and the CRITICAL rows coherently read the particle as both continuation and scene-shift.

words.root_display: not applicable; temporal particle with no lexical root
words.gloss_range: certain temporal condition governing the gathering protasis and the two verdict clauses
words.prose: {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}) makes the gathering a when-frame, not a doubtful if-frame. It governs the passive gathering clause and opens space for the two later state clauses as the answer. The payoff is modal as well as temporal: the ayah treats the assembly as certain, then makes hostility and denial unfold as the guaranteed consequence.

topics.headline: certain temporal protasis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the gathering is assumed as certain, and the hostile verdicts are framed as its guaranteed consequence.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify a conditional-temporal frame headed by {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}), and the following clauses supply the response.

words.gloss_range: passive perfect of being gathered or assembled, locally selected for eschatological gathering under a certain temporal frame
words.root_gloss_range: gathering, herding, crowding, and resurrection assembly; local form selects passive eschatological assembly while retaining pressure of driven aggregation
words.prose: {{ar:حُشِرَ}} ({{tr:ḥushira}}) opens the event before naming the people who undergo it. The passive form leaves the gatherer unspoken and makes the assembled population the grammatical focus. Its root field adds the sense of driven crowding, while the certain-time frame makes the passive perfect feel like a fixed judgment snapshot rather than a speculative future scene.

topics.headline: passive certain gathering
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the gatherer is withheld while the act of being assembled becomes the unavoidable opening fact.
topics.reason: The local verb is passive perfect under the temporal frame, and attachment evidence explicitly marks the agent as unexpressed.

topics.headline: driven assembly root pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the selected sense is judgment-gathering, but the root still makes the scene feel like compelled crowding into one public reckoning.
topics.reason: The local context selects eschatological assembly, while broader root senses of herding and crowding remain as controlled image-pressure rather than separate active meanings.

topics.headline: event-first formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb strikes first: the event frames the people before any later verdict about worship is heard.
topics.reason: The verb precedes its passive subject and the contextual profile marks this passive form as a small judgment-gathering set.

words.gloss_range: definite human collective functioning as the passive subject of the gathering
words.root_gloss_range: human beings as a social and perceptive collective; derivational dispute with forgetfulness remains interpretive pressure, not a replacement for the local noun
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلنَّاسُ}} ({{tr:al-nāsu}}) names the gathered party after the passive event has already landed. Its nominative role makes humanity the visible bearer of the gathering, while its definiteness gives the scene a generic, all-human scale. The human-root background adds social exposure and perception, with the recorded forgetfulness derivation only as a secondary pressure: the ayah gathers people publicly before the worship relation is reversed. The same human frame also links this public gathering to the surah's later personal and collective human scenes (46:15; 46:18).

topics.headline: definite passive human subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that humanity is grammatically gathered as a definite collective, not introduced as scattered private worshippers.
topics.reason: The noun is nominative and definite, and attachment evidence identifies it as the passive subject of {{ar:حُشِرَ}} ({{tr:ḥushira}}).

topics.headline: social-perceptive human frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the gathered humans are a social-perceptive collective, while the derivational dispute only colors the scene rather than changing the local reference.
topics.reason: The local form means people/humankind; root-family and disputed derivation add controlled human-framing pressure without overriding the noun's ordinary referent.

topics.headline: surah human assembly thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this human collective becomes the audience for the two verdicts and also belongs to the surah's wider human-placement thread (46:15; 46:18).
topics.reason: The same-surah references (46:15; 46:18) are concrete and the local syntax makes the gathered humans the population before the verdict clauses.

words.gloss_range: perfect plural being-verb in the apodosis, locally predicating hostile status of the invoked entities
words.root_gloss_range: being, becoming, and coming-to-be; local use is copular/predicative with state-instantiation pressure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: certain temporal condition governing the verdict clauses

words.prose: {{ar:كَانُوا۟}} ({{tr:kānū}}) begins the answer to the when-clause. Its perfect form, under {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}), makes the future verdict sound settled, and its hidden plural subject resumes the invoked entities from 46:5. The being-root is not empty here: it installs a realized hostile state, then prepares the same subject for the repeated state clause so enmity and denial become a sealed two-part verdict.

topics.headline: future-certain hidden subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the invoked entities from 46:5 are carried silently into the judgment scene as the subject of the hostile predicate.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence resolves the 3mp subject to the invoked entities from 46:5 and places the verb under the temporal condition.

topics.headline: being as hostile state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb does not merely sit between subject and predicate; it realizes the worshipped entities as enemies.
topics.reason: The local grammar is copular, so broader formation senses are narrowed to state-instantiation pressure around the enemy predicate.

topics.headline: doubled verdict frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first state clause is built to be repeated, so enmity and denial become a two-part verdict.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence marks the second {{ar:كَانُوا۟}} ({{tr:kānū}}) as coordinated with this one, supporting the CRITICAL doubled-verdict reading.

words.root_display: not applicable; preposition with no lexical root
words.gloss_range: preposition governing the target pronoun and directing the enemy predicate against that target

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: enemy predicate that makes the prepositional target adversative

words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la-}}) turns the enemy predicate into a directed relation. Beside {{ar:أَعْدَآءً}} ({{tr:aʿdāʾan}}), the usually relational or benefactive-looking preposition works adversatively: enemies to them, effectively against them. Its placement before the enemy noun makes the harmed party audible before the hostility lands.

topics.headline: adversative target lām
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that enmity is not abstract; the preposition points the hostility toward the worshippers.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the pronoun a governed complement linked with the enemy predicate, supporting an adversative target relation.

topics.headline: compact target before predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the clause's order: the target is heard before the enemy label, so the reversal is directed before it is named.
topics.reason: The local sequence places the prepositional phrase before the predicate and the CRITICAL sound row supports the same directed staging.

words.root_display: not applicable; pronoun with no lexical root
words.gloss_range: third-person masculine plural pronoun governed by the preceding preposition, locally referring to the gathered worshippers

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: first state verb whose hidden subject is distinct from the target pronoun

words.prose: {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) is small, but it carries the two-party reversal. The context selects the gathered worshippers as the target: the invoked entities become enemies to them. Because the subject of {{ar:كَانُوا۟}} ({{tr:kānū}}) is the worshipped entities, this pronoun keeps the harmed party distinct, and its sound later recurs in the possessed worship phrase.

topics.headline: target pronoun resolution
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the pronoun is not the hidden subject; it marks the people against whom the invoked entities turn.
topics.reason: The bundle explicitly resolves {{ar:لَهُمْ}} ({{tr:lahum}}) to the gathered people, so ambiguity survives only as a translation-risk warning.

topics.headline: compressed and echoed target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the target is compressed into a suffix and then echoed by the later worship suffix.
topics.reason: The pronoun is attached to the preposition and the later possessed worship phrase repeats the same plural pronoun sound.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative plural enemy predicate in the first state clause
words.root_gloss_range: enmity, hostility, transgression, and crossing beyond bounds; local word selects enemy-status while retaining overstepping pressure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: state verb governing the enemy predicate

words.prose: {{ar:أَعْدَآءً}} ({{tr:aʿdāʾan}}) is the first verdict word. As an indefinite accusative predicate of {{ar:كَانُوا۟}} ({{tr:kānū}}), it makes enmity the hidden subject's state without specifying one limited form of hostility. The root's crossing-over pressure sharpens the reversal: those treated as objects of devotion cross into the role of adversaries, and this first landing prepares the final denial predicate.

topics.headline: indefinite enemy predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that enmity is a grammatical verdict-state and remains open in kind, not a named class of known enemies.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the word as the accusative predicate of the first {{ar:كَانُوا۟}} ({{tr:kānū}}) clause.

topics.headline: hostile reversal root pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the enemy sense is selected, while the older crossing-beyond sense makes the devotion-to-hostility reversal feel like a boundary violation.
topics.reason: The local predicate means enemies; broader motion/transgression senses are valid only as image-pressure attached to that selected sense.

topics.headline: first half of binary verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this first predicate names relational rupture before the ayah moves to denial of worship.
topics.reason: The repeated state-clause structure supports a two-verdict reading: enemy relation first, worship-denial second.

words.root_display: not applicable; particle with no lexical root
words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction launching the second state clause
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps the second verdict coordinated with the first. It does not make the denial clause a loose afterthought; it joins two complete state clauses while allowing the second to explain the kind of enmity just named. The repeated cadence makes the judgment cumulative: enemies, and deniers concerning the worship.

topics.headline: coordinated second verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that denial is an equal second verdict and also specifies the nature of the enmity.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the second {{ar:كَانُوا۟}} ({{tr:kānū}}) clause as coordinated with the first, matching the CRITICAL coordination and reprise rows.

words.gloss_range: repeated perfect plural being-verb governing the final denial predicate
words.root_gloss_range: being, becoming, and state predication; local use repeats the same hidden subject and assigns a worship-domain denial state
words.prose: {{ar:كَانُوا۟}} ({{tr:kānū}}) deliberately reprises the earlier being-verb. The hidden subject is still the invoked entities, but the intervening worship phrase redirects the second state from hostility toward persons to denial concerning worship. This repetition gives the final charge the same predicative weight as the first, while the fronted domain phrase delays the last word.

topics.headline: same-subject second state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same invoked entities receive a second fixed state, not a new subject or a new scene.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence resolves the second 3mp subject as the same as the first and identifies {{ar:كَٰفِرِينَ}} ({{tr:kāfirīna}}) as its predicate.

topics.headline: fronted worship domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that worship is placed before the denial predicate, so the final charge is heard as domain-specific repudiation.
topics.reason: The governed phrase precedes the final predicate in the second {{ar:كَانُوا۟}} ({{tr:kānū}}) clause, making the denial domain explicit.

topics.headline: reprise and polemical thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the exact verbal reprise that gives the ayah its balanced two-stroke judgment rhythm.
topics.reason: The local repetition is direct and the contextual evidence allows a nearby polemical thread around this wording without making it control the parse.

words.root_display: not applicable; preposition with no lexical root
words.gloss_range: preposition governing the worship gerund and scoping the final denial to that domain

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: final denial predicate scoped by the governed worship phrase

words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}}) makes the final denial targeted. It governs the worship noun and places that governed phrase before {{ar:كَٰفِرِينَ}} ({{tr:kāfirīna}}), so the reader hears the domain before the rejecting predicate. The particle can carry topical and causal pressure here, but the local grammar keeps the core sense clear: the denial concerns the worship relation itself.

topics.headline: scoped worship domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final predicate is not generic disbelief; it is denial concerning the worship itself, with causal pressure kept secondary.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the phrase as a governed complement of the final predicate, while the topical/causal range is preserved only within that local scope.

topics.headline: fronted bound phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the attached preposition fuses with the worship noun and pushes the denied domain ahead of the final word.
topics.reason: The local written and syntactic form creates a compact governed phrase before the predicate.

words.gloss_range: possessed worship/service gerund governed by the preceding preposition as the domain of denial
words.root_gloss_range: worship, service, devotion, servitude, and subjugation-family pressure; local word selects worship-service while leaving the possessed relation grammatically charged
words.prose: {{ar:عِبَادَتِهِمْ}} ({{tr:ʿibādatihim}}) is the worship-domain that the final predicate denies. As a governed gerund in construct with the suffix, it is not worship in general but their worship, a possessed relation now exposed for repudiation. The suffix permits controlled subjective and objective pressure: the worshippers' act and worship directed toward the invoked entities both feed the reversal, while the broader service and servitude range makes the denied relation heavier than a momentary ritual gesture. Its compact gerund form stands before the final denial, and the closing pronoun sound echoes the earlier target pronoun, binding the people harmed by enmity to the worship being denied.

topics.headline: governed possessed worship domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the denial targets a definite possessed worship relation, not worship as an abstract idea.
topics.reason: The noun is governed by {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}}) and carries a possessive suffix resolved in the bundle to the people whose worship is being denied.

topics.headline: genitive ambiguity and servitude range
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase can pressure both the worshippers' act and the worship directed around the worshipped entities, while the selected sense remains worship-service.
topics.reason: The construct suffix supports subjective/objective routing, but local grammar and the final predicate keep the main sense as a worship-service domain.

topics.headline: worship-denial thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah escalates prior calling (46:5) into worship-service and then makes that whole relation the object of denial.
topics.reason: The local phrase stands between enemy and denier predicates, and the concrete same-surah boundary evidence links it back to the invocation scene in 46:5.

topics.headline: form and echo position
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the compact gerund is placed before the final denial and echoes the earlier target pronoun.
topics.reason: The local form is a gerund/maṣdar and its position before the final predicate is syntactically forced by the governed phrase.

words.gloss_range: indefinite masculine plural active-participle predicate naming denial or covering with respect to the worship phrase
words.root_gloss_range: covering, ingratitude, rejection, denial, and repudiation; local predicate selects denial/repudiation while retaining covering and disowning pressure
words.prose: {{ar:كَٰفِرِينَ}} ({{tr:kāfirīna}}) closes the ayah as the final state predicate. The active participle makes denial a sustained condition of the same hidden plural subject, and the preceding worship phrase gives that denial its target. The root's covering and ingratitude range sharpens the local denial: the worshipped entities cover over and repudiate the worship relation, so a familiar label for rejecters is inverted onto the very recipients of false devotion.

topics.headline: participial denial state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word names a sustained predicate-state, not a one-time denial act.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the word as an active participle in the accusative predicate slot of the second {{ar:كَانُوا۟}} ({{tr:kānū}}) clause.

topics.headline: denial-covering range
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that denial is primary, while covering and ingratitude make the repudiation feel like disowning the worship relation itself.
topics.reason: The local governed phrase selects denial concerning worship, while broader root branches remain as semantic pressure rather than independent senses.

topics.headline: role inversion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the reversal: the term lands on the worshipped entities, not on the worshippers alone.
topics.reason: The hidden subject remains the invoked entities, so the predicate's familiar rejecter-label function is locally reassigned to the worshipped objects.

topics.headline: climactic final verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah's last heard word is the denial verdict after gathering, enmity, and worship-domain fronting.
topics.reason: The word is final in the ayah and completes the second coordinated state clause, so closure weight and structural resolution are locally licensed.

variants.scope_en: Human beings or human presence: ins, humans, people, anasi, insan as a person or group, and anis meaning anyone present in a dwelling.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The passive gathering, the twice-realized states, the enemy predicate, and the denial of the worship relation.
baseline_models.mechanism: Forced co-presence reverses the relation sought through worship: its recipients become opposing parties and expressly sever themselves from the devotion directed to them.

activation_trace.role: A group is driven together toward one destination, supplying the compulsory encounter in which the relation is tested.
Occurrence and presence in time make both hostility and repudiation realized states rather than remote possibilities.
The opponent of an ally supplies the direct reversal from presumed patronage to hostility.
Submissive devotion names the prior bond whose expected reciprocity collapses.
Explicit disavowal supplies the act by which the recipients cut themselves loose from that bond.

changed_reading.before: The verse merely predicts that hostile beings will deny a past cult at resurrection.
changed_reading.after: The gathering is a forced relational reckoning: the very recipients from whom alliance was sought reverse position and repudiate the worship that joined the parties.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The worship noun is placed between enemy-making and repudiation, allowing non-ritual power images within its root inventory to remain active.
baseline_models.mechanism: Worship can be carried as a double abasement: devotees submit themselves while also trying to tame, employ, or bind a recipient into serving their needs. Assembly exposes that arrangement as an overreach, so the would-be instrument becomes an adversary.

activation_trace.role: The root's making-someone-servile image exposes a latent attempt to turn the worshipped recipient into an instrument.
Taming and smoothing something for use adds the functional expectation hidden inside the devotional relation.
Crossing a rightful limit marks the attempted power arrangement as transgressive and explains its reversal.
Blocking acknowledged truth makes the final denial an exposure of what the arrangement had concealed.

changed_reading.before: Worship is only a ritual act that its object later rejects.
changed_reading.after: Worship also encodes a failed power bargain: self-abasement sought leverage over a patron, and the attempted instrument refuses that role as an adversary.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The people-root's mapped seeing inventory, gathering, temporal presence, and covering/disavowal converge on public exposure.
baseline_models.mechanism: Assembly does more than collect bodies. It brings perceivers, opponents, and a previously covered relation into one visible present, where denial itself reveals who was never an ally.

activation_trace.role: Perception by sight, hearing, or felt awareness makes the human collective the field in which concealed relations become perceptible.
Directed collection removes separation and stages a shared disclosure.
Presence in a determinate time turns latent allegiance into an observable state.
Covering supplies the hidden condition that the gathered confrontation brings to light.
Open opposition is the disclosed reality beneath the presumed alliance.

changed_reading.before: Gathering is only transport into a later crowd.
changed_reading.after: Gathering is an epistemic exposure: co-presence makes the covered truth of the worship relation visible as opposition and disavowal.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding call receives no reply across an extended horizon because its addressees are inattentive; the focus scene then supplies a grim delayed response, in which the first decisive reciprocity is hostility and repudiation.

activation_trace.role: Calling by speech supplies both the repeated address and the relational pull that seeks a respondent.
A verbal answer is explicitly the missing link, turning the focus repudiation into a possible terminal reply.
An extended span of time holds the nonresponse open until the gathering horizon.
Inattention leaves the invocation outside awareness and explains the present silence.
The eventual response takes the relational form of opposition rather than alliance.
Disavowal provides the content of that delayed response.
Devotion is the relation about which the answer is finally given.

structural_cues: 46:5 immediately precedes the focus and moves from repeated invocation through nonresponse to a stated time limit; 46:6 opens with the gathering condition.
The same third-person parties persist across the verse boundary, making a delayed call-and-answer reading grammatically available.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies calling, absent response, inattention, a temporal horizon, and then hostility plus disavowal; I infer that the focus event functions as the call's delayed answer. A live alternative is that the two verses only list separate failures without forming one communication arc.

changed_reading.before: The focus begins an independent scene in which former cult objects suddenly become hostile.
changed_reading.after: The focus completes an unanswered invocation: after prolonged silence, the only decisive answer the worshipper receives is adversarial repudiation.

context_deltas.mechanism: Denial migrates across the relation. People first cover or knowingly reject signs and recode them as deception or fabrication; in the focus, the worshipped parties take up the denying position and reject the worshippers' claim upon them.

activation_trace.role: Rejection of manifest truth establishes denial first as the worshippers' own posture.
Diversion and deception supply the recoding by which what appears clear is dismissed.
Invented falsehood supplies the accusation used to sever a message from its claimed source.
Denial despite knowledge sharpens the earlier posture from mere ignorance to willful repudiation.
The focus transfers repudiation to the worshipped side of the relation.
Hostility is the relational consequence when the denier's own logic returns from the opposite party.

structural_cues: 46:7-11 repeatedly stage hostile renaming of a clear message; 46:26 recalls knowing rejection; the focus places denial in the mouths or stance of the invoked parties instead.
The reversal preserves denial as the repeated action while changing who performs it and what claim is denied.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two differently directed denials and several false renamings; I infer a mimetic reversal in which the worshippers' repudiating practice returns from their supposed allies. The alternative is simple thematic repetition with no transfer between agents.

changed_reading.before: The worshipped parties' denial is an isolated declaration about cultic acts.
changed_reading.after: Their denial mirrors and reverses the worshippers' own habit of recoding truth: repudiation changes sides and becomes the mechanism of enmity.

context_deltas.mechanism: The gathered confrontation behaves like a hearing. An enemy branch can denote seeking redress from an authority; witnesses state what they know, deeds are rendered without deficit, parties are presented, and speech fixes the record. The recipients' disavowal therefore functions as adverse testimony, not only emotion.

activation_trace.role: Knowledge stated as testimony supplies the evidentiary function later assigned to the recipients' denial.
Full rendering without shortfall turns the hearing toward exact settlement of what was done.
Bringing parties out for inspection supplies the public presentation frame.
Spoken answer fixes acknowledgment within that presentation.
A wronged party's appeal for official redress converts generic enmity into an adverse legal position.
Disavowal becomes the negative testimony that defeats the worshippers' asserted relation.
The devotional conduct is the disputed relation entered into the record.

structural_cues: The surah moves through witness language, graded deeds, full settlement, and two scenes of presentation before the focus's relational claims are finally evaluated.
The focus combines a plural adverse party with an explicit denial of a past relation, a shape compatible with contested testimony.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies witness, exact settlement, public presentation, speech, and a legal-redress branch inside the focus enemy root; I infer a hearing in which repudiation operates as adverse evidence. Literal personal hostility remains a live, compatible alternative rather than being displaced.

changed_reading.before: Enemies are simply antagonists who dislike the worshippers.
changed_reading.after: They are adverse parties in a public reckoning, and their denial of worship is testimony that legally undoes the alliance the worshippers thought they possessed.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus enemy form has packet-supplied split mappings to return and counting. Contextual recompense, intentional work, degree-by-degree differentiation, and full payment activate those non-dominant branches: acts of worship can return as itemized adversarial counterparts at assembly.

activation_trace.role: Matching an act with its consequence supplies the return mechanism for prior conduct.
Purposeful action identifies what can persist into the later settlement.
Movement by successive degrees makes the settlement differentiated rather than generic.
Completion without deficiency supplies exactness to the return of the acts.
Return after departure makes the former devotional investment come back into the encounter.
Enumeration makes each returned attachment legible as a countable liability.
A counterpart counted alongside another allows an act or attachment to stand opposite its maker.
The devotional acts provide the concrete conduct that returns for settlement.

structural_cues: 46:14-20 repeatedly connect what parties did with differentiated recompense and complete rendering.
The focus uses plural adversaries and a plural possessive relation, which can carry an itemized plurality without requiring it.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies explicit accounting language and split focus mappings to return and enumeration; I infer that prior worship can reappear as an adversarial liability. This is form-distant and the ordinary referent remains worshipped beings, so the accounting reading should coexist as an exploratory overlay only.

changed_reading.before: Only external worshipped beings return as enemies.
changed_reading.after: The worship itself can be heard as returning in countable form: each invested attachment stands opposite the worshipper as a fully rendered liability.

context_deltas.mechanism: An apparent cloud is welcomed as rain but proves to be a destroying wind; shortly afterward, the aid root carries a rain-and-relief branch precisely where adopted gods fail to help. This material reversal lets enemy describe a trusted affordance becoming harmful or absent, not only a conscious feeling.

activation_trace.role: Something appearing from one direction supplies the initially promising but underdetermined sign.
Sought rain or rain-like good supplies the benefit projected onto the approaching phenomenon.
The literal movement of air replaces the expected water-bearing benefit with a different material agent.
Comprehensive ruin supplies the harmful outcome of the misread promise.
The root's rain-as-relief image joins the expected weather benefit to the later question of failed aid.
Opposition names the endpoint when what was trusted for benefit instead harms or abandons.
Repudiation is the relational equivalent of the material promise failing at the moment of need.

structural_cues: 46:24-25 reverse an anticipated benefit into destruction; 46:28 then asks why proximity-gods supplied no aid.
The two reversals share an expectation-of-relief structure even though one concerns weather and the other patronage.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the misread cloud, destructive wind, failed divine aid, and a branch that couples aid with rain-relief; I infer a shared affordance-reversal mechanism. The live alternative is that the weather episode and patronage failure are adjacent but mechanically independent.

changed_reading.before: Becoming enemies means that personal agents acquire hostile intent.
changed_reading.after: Enmity can also be functional reversal: what was approached as a source of relief discloses itself as harm or as total non-help.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later recap describes gods deliberately adopted as means of proximity, asks why they gave no aid, and says they were lost from their users. Worship is thus a transaction meant to secure nearness and patronage; the focus shows its terminal reversal into abandonment and disavowal.

activation_trace.role: Deliberate adoption or acquisition supplies the worshippers' active construction of the patronage relation.
An offering used for approach supplies the promised access that motivates the transaction.
Aid and vindicating support name the expected return that never arrives.
Loss of the supposed patrons supplies practical abandonment at the decisive moment.
Devotion is the consideration invested in hopes of proximity and support.
The expected ally's opposite names the transaction's final relational result.
Disavowal cancels the worshippers' claim that the investment created a valid bond.

structural_cues: 46:28 restates the same invoked parties in transactional order: adoption, approach, expected aid, disappearance, and exposure of fabrication.
The focus supplies the face-to-face outcome that the recap's failed aid leaves implicit.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adopted proximity-gods, expected help, disappearance, and focus repudiation; I infer that worship was expected to purchase access and patronage. A live alternative is that proximity names only ritual classification and not a consciously transactional motive.

changed_reading.before: Worship creates a vague attachment that later fails.
changed_reading.after: Worship is exposed as a failed proximity-for-aid transaction: the adopted patrons vanish when needed and then deny that the investment ever bound them.

context_deltas.mechanism: A successful address circuit appears after the failed cult: hearers comprehend, hold attentive silence, turn toward their people, relay the call, and demand a response; absence of other patrons closes the contrast. The focus worship is therefore readable as a broken communication circuit whose only ultimate feedback is denial.

activation_trace.role: Hearing that becomes understanding and compliance initiates a genuinely responsive circuit.
Attentive silence is receptive rather than the inattentive silence surrounding the false invocation.
Turning one's face toward a destination supplies the directed relay from reception to community.
Returning an answer is the response demanded from the next hearers in the chain.
The call draws hearers toward a claimant and provides the signal that the circuit carries.
Patronal love and aid define the reciprocal support unavailable outside the successful response.
Devotion is recast as sustained address seeking receptive allegiance.
Repudiation is the failed circuit's final negative feedback.
The nonresponsive addressee resolves as an opponent rather than a patron.

structural_cues: 46:29-32 forms a reception-to-relay sequence, while 46:5-6 forms invocation-to-nonresponse-to-repudiation.
Both sequences use calling and answering vocabulary but yield opposite social networks: warning and response versus false patronage and enmity.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two address sequences with opposite outcomes; I infer that the later successful relay diagnoses the focus worship as failed reciprocity. The alternative is that the later sequence illustrates belief generally without commenting on the mechanics of worship in the focus.

changed_reading.before: Worship is a static cultic label, and enmity is its unrelated future punishment.
changed_reading.after: Worship is a failed address network: unlike receptive hearing that becomes response and relay, its calls terminate in silence and finally return as repudiation.

context_deltas.mechanism: Resurrection overcomes the powerlessness of death, presentation exposes parties to inspection, reality is verbally acknowledged, and prior duration contracts to a brief stay. Against that frame, the focus's repeated being-root marks a phase change: hidden relational roles become presently actual at gathering.

activation_trace.role: Loss of life and power supplies the state crossed when the gathered encounter becomes possible.
Exposure for inspection makes the new relational states public and testable.
Stable correspondence with reality supplies what the public acknowledgment confirms.
Remaining in a place supplies the duration that the closing comparison radically compresses.
Twice-stated occurrence and temporal presence actualize hostility and denial at the threshold event.
Directed gathering supplies the threshold at which latent roles become present.
Opposition is one of the relational states actualized by the threshold.

structural_cues: 46:33 states the transition from death to life; 46:34 repeats public presentation; 46:35 collapses remembered duration to a brief interval.
The focus repeats the being-root on both sides of the conjunction, rhythmically marking two simultaneous state realizations.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies resurrection, presentation, acknowledged reality, compressed duration, and repeated temporal-state predicates; I infer that gathering actualizes previously hidden roles. The alternative is ordinary past/future predication with no special phase-transition force in the repeated verb.

changed_reading.before: The two predicates simply describe what the parties will feel and say later.
changed_reading.after: The gathering is a state-change threshold: presumed allies are publicly actualized as opponents and repudiators once ordinary time and concealment lose their hold.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This cross-spatial reading uses distant but explicit focus branches: worship can scatter into many directions while gathering can evoke compacted form. It remains anchored in the worship and gathering roots and clarifies their opposition, but downstream prose should present it as a material analogy, not as the lexical sense of either surface form.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The gathering root and the worship root contain opposed images of compaction and dispersal.

activation_trace.role: Dispersal into multiple directions turns misdirected devotions into spatially divergent paths.
A tightly packed bodily form supplies the compression that gathering imposes on those divergent paths.
Opposition is what becomes visible once the dispersed paths are forced into one encounter.

changed_reading.before: Only human bodies are collected at the gathering.
changed_reading.after: The event also compresses worship's scattered directions into one confrontation, where every divergent path resolves into opposition.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The optical projection is surprising because it comes from the people-root's non-dominant mapped eye-image branch, not from ordinary syntax. It remains anchored in that supplied focus mapping plus covering, worship, and enmity, but should be rendered only as a reflexive analogy: it does not establish that the pronouns denote psychological projections.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The mapped inventory for the people-root includes the human figure seen in the eye, beside worship, covering, and opposition.

activation_trace.role: The miniature human figure reflected in the pupil supplies an image of the worshipper encountering a projected likeness.
Devotion directs attachment toward the projected recipient.
Covering allows the worshipper's contribution to the image to remain unrecognized until confrontation.
The reflected construction returns as an opponent rather than confirming the self that invested it.

changed_reading.before: An entirely external object independently turns against the worshipper.
changed_reading.after: As an optical analogy, the worshipper meets a magnified projection of human desire that refuses recognition and returns as an adversarial mirror.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This social analogy is surprising because the parent-child episode does not change the focus pronouns' antecedent. It remains useful through the focus's worship-to-enmity reversal and the context's sustained burden followed by filial disgust, but downstream prose must call it an analogy of asymmetric investment, never a claim that children are the worshipped parties.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus reverses a heavily invested asymmetric bond into hostility and repudiation.

activation_trace.role: Interior bearing and pregnancy supply prolonged embodied investment in a dependent relation.
Hardship borne despite aversion measures the cost invested in that relation.
Parenthood preserves the asymmetric giver-recipient relation across the contextual contrast.
A voiced sign of disgust supplies the shocking repudiation returned by the dependent party.
Sustained devotion supplies the focus's asymmetrical investment.
Opposition supplies the reversal returned by the recipient of that investment.
Disavowal completes the analogy by refusing the bond on which the giver relied.

changed_reading.before: The focus reversal concerns only a doctrinally false cult relation.
changed_reading.after: As a social analogy, it exposes a broader terror of asymmetric investment: long service cannot compel recognition, and the recipient may answer dependence with repudiation.

strongest_changes: 46:5 turns hostility and disavowal into the only delayed answer to a long-unanswered invocation.
Witness, full-settlement, and presentation cues recast the recipients as adverse parties whose denial functions as testimony.
46:28 exposes worship as a failed proximity-for-aid transaction, while 46:29-32 contrast it with a genuinely responsive relay.
The split enemy-root mappings preserve an exploratory reading in which worship returns as an itemized liability.
summary.what_was_special: The focus proved unusually relational: silence becomes a delayed negative answer, presumed patronage becomes adverse testimony, expected relief reverses into harm, and non-dominant return/count branches keep the worship itself active as something that can come back against its practitioner.
remaining_uncertainties: The precise antecedent of the plural parties is supplied by local discourse but remains grammatically less explicit inside the focus ayah alone.
The accounting/return model depends on legitimate packet mappings that are form-distant from the dominant enemy sense and should remain exploratory.
The weather-to-patronage mechanism may be deliberate lexical activation or only a strong adjacency-based analogy.
The power-bargain baseline depends on extending worship-root images of subjugation and taming into motive, not on ordinary ritual syntax alone.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Gathering reverses devotional proximity into opposition.** ح ش ر B001 is gathering and driving a group to a destination; ع د و B003 is enemy and enmity, with B001 retaining overstepping into injustice. The same parties linked by worship are forced into one venue and become adversaries. I infer that gathering removes the distance that had concealed the relation’s asymmetry. The ayah reads as an exposure mechanism: proximity reveals that the supposed alliance was structurally hostile.
2. **`كافرين` as explicit disavowal.** ك ف ر B005 is disavowal, directly suited to `بعبادتهم كافرين`. The construction attaches repudiation to the worship itself, not merely to a proposition. I infer a reversal of testimony: those treated as worshipped parties deny that the relation bound them. The ayah therefore preserves disbelief but activates juridical repudiation of the devotees’ claim.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 46:28 supplied the historical analogue: the mediators fail to aid and disappear before the final gathering. That later failure made `كافرين` as disavowal (ك ف ر B005) more specific than a generic statement of unbelief.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Gathering is forced relational disclosure.** `حُشِرَ` activates ح ش ر B001, collecting while driving a group from its place toward a destination. The two occurrences of `كَانُوا` (ك و ن B001) bracket two states that then occur openly: enemies and disavowers. Before this, 46:4-5 exposes an unsupported share and unanswered calls; after it, 46:7-10 repeatedly stages truth, witness, and opposed reactions. The packet supplies displacement into a common venue and explicit changed predicates; I infer that forced co-presence removes the spatial and temporal conditions that allowed the imagined relationship to remain unfalsified. The gathering therefore functions as an adjudicative exposure of what the relationship always amounted to.

2. **The final `كَٰفِرِينَ` is precise repudiation, not a generic label.** Because its complement is `بِعِبَادَتِهِمْ`, ك ف ر B005, disavowal and declaring oneself free of an association, is activated beside B001, covering; `عِبَادَتِهِمْ` anchors ع ب د B003, submissive obedience and worship, with B006 supplying the honor/service bestowed on the object. Ayah 46:4 framed that service as an unproved partnership, and 46:5 showed its recipient absent from the response circuit. The packet gives bestowed honor and explicit severance; I infer that the objects reject the agency and title projected onto them. The close reads as cancellation of the worshippers’ claimed affiliation, which then makes `أَعْدَآءً` (ع د و B003) a legal-social reversal from supposed ally to adverse party.

3. **Enmity exposes worship as a crossed boundary.** `أَعْدَآءً` also activates ع د و B001, overstepping a bound into injustice. In 46:4, `شِرْك` assigns a share without evidence; in 46:5, invocation treats the lower substitute as capable of response. The packet supplies the unauthorized share and the resultant enemy status; I supply the causal arrow that projection of divine capacity onto another party violates the boundary of that party as well as the divine claim. The ayah then reads not only as abandonment by false allies but as the emergence of a grievance generated by the worship itself.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 46:10 sharpened the difference between a projected relation and a warranted one: the witness bears knowledge-based testimony through ش ه د B002 and then trusts, whereas the objects at 46:6 reject the role assigned to them. The later witness made forced gathering read as exposure of unsupported attribution, not hostility emerging without a prior relational defect.

baseline.text: İnsanlar toplandığında onlar kendilerine düşman olacak ve kendilerine kulluk edildiğini inkâr edecekler.

findings.text: Zorla aynı yerde toplanma, uzaktan kurulmuş sahte yakınlığın örttüğü eşitsizliği kaldırır ve sözde ittifakın gerçekte düşmanca olduğunu açığa çıkarır.
İlahî yetkiyi başka bir tarafa yükleyen kulluk, o tarafın sınırını da aşarak sonradan düşmanlık biçiminde ortaya çıkan bir hak ihlali üretir.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A claimed relation is exposed by whether a call completes a response circuit and whether the claimed party remains allied under assembly.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The latent imagery recasts theology as a failed communication system followed by a public reversal of roles.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Gathering converts objects of worship into adversaries
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Human claimants and invoked figures are driven into one assembly, where presumed service and alliance reverse into hostility and disavowal.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: Driven gathering (`quranic:root_000324:B001/m01`); an enemy or adversary (`quranic:root_000993:B003/m01`); worship as obedience (`quranic:root_000973:B003/m01`); explicit disavowal (`quranic:root_001307:B005/m01`); human visibility against hiddenness (`quranic:root_000059:B001/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: `إذا حشر الناس` (46:6), `كانوا لهم أعداء` (46:6), and `كانوا بعبادتهم كافرين` (46:6).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Assembly makes the failed relation visible: what had been treated as obedient access is disclosed as mutual opposition.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir topluluğu yalnızca bir arada bulunmuş saymaktan öte, onu bulunduğu yerden çıkarıp belirli bir hedefe doğru sürerek toplamayı açıkça bildirir. Büyük son toplanma, toplanma yeri ve insanları önden götüren kişi de bu işlemin ad, yer ve yapan kişi uzantılarıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal tek bir kişinin hareketini ya da küçük kara hayvanlarını değil, bir topluluğun yönlendirilerek bir araya getirilmesini kapsar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın toplama ve sevk etme çekirdeğini korurken gün, yer, yapan kişi ve savaşa çıkarma gibi kalıba bağlı kullanımları ayrı yüzler olarak gösterir.

concept_map.definition: Bir topluluğu bulunduğu yerden çıkarıp belirli bir hedefe doğru sevk ederek bir araya getirmektir. Bütün insanların son kez toplanması, toplanılan yer ve insanları toplayıp önden götüren kişi bu çekirdeğe bağlı kullanımlardır.

facets.statement: Birden çok kişiyi bulundukları yerden çıkararak aynı hedefe doğru sevk edip toplama.
Bütün insanların yeniden dirilişle birlikte son bir buluşma yerine toplanması ve bu toplanmanın günü ya da yeri.
İnsanları toplayan, sevk eden veya onların önünde toplanma yerine doğru ilerleyen kişi.
Bir topluluğu savaş gibi belirli bir amaç için yerinden çıkarma; olumsuz kalıpta savaşa çıkarmama.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, çekirdeği topluluğun bir hedefe doğru sevk edilerek bir araya getirilmesi olarak ortaklaşa verir. Son büyük toplanma, buluşma yeri ve toplayıp önden götüren kişi bu işlem çevresinde adlaşan kullanımlardır. Olumsuz kalıpta kadınların savaşa çıkarılmaması da tanıklanan dar bir kullanımdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Topluluğun hem bir araya getirilmesini hem de belirli bir hedefe doğru yöneltilmesini birlikte anlatan çekirdek karşılıktır.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه قولهم حشرتهم السنة أو حشرت مالهم، أي أضرّت بهم، جمعتهم إلى الأمصار، أذهبت المال، أهلكته، أو أزالته عنهم.
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس هو الحشر العام للجماعات إلا من جهة كونه تطبيقا مجازيا أو اصطلاحيا، وليس اسم الحشرات.
branches.source_phrase_ar: حشرت مال بني فلان السنة كأنها جمعته ذهبت به وأتت عليه (maqayis)؛ حشرتهم السنة تضمهم من النواحي إلى الأمصار (ayn;tahdhib)؛ حشرتهم السنة إذا أصابهم الضر حتى يهبطوا الأمصار (jamhara)؛ حشرت السنة مال فلان أي أهلكته (sihah)؛ حشرت السنة مال بني فلان أي أزالته عنهم (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi belirli hayvanların bu eylemini ölüm olarak açıklar, ancak anlatımı bir görüş veya aktarım olarak sınırlar. Bu nedenle ölüm okuması korunur fakat kökün genel ve bağımsız anlamı gibi sunulamaz.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Ölüm anlamı yalnızca tanıklanan hayvan bağlamına ve aktarılan yoruma aittir; genel toplama dalının yerine geçmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, belirli hayvanları konu alan tanıklı söz öbeğiyle sınırlıdır ve yalın biçime genel bir ölüm anlamı yüklemez.

concept_map.definition: Belirli hayvanlardan söz eden tanıklı kullanımda, onların ölmesi demektir. Kaynakların aktarım kaydıyla verdiği bu okuma genel bir toplama veya genel bir ölüm fiili değildir.

facets.statement: Belirli hayvanların söz konusu edildiği kalıpta eylemin onların ölümü diye yorumlanması.
Okumanın kesin ve genel bir tanım olarak değil, aktarılan bir görüş veya rivayet olarak kaydedilmesi.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar hayvanlara bağlı bu kullanımı ölüm diye açıklar; bunlardan biri açıklamayı açıkça aktarılmış bir görüş olarak sunar. Dolayısıyla tanıklık vardır, fakat genel anlam düzeyine çıkarılmamalıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Yalnızca tanıklanan hayvan bağlamındaki aktarılmış ölüm okumasını doğal Türkçeyle karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Hayvan katılımcıları ile ölüm sonucunu, dar bağlam sınırı içinde korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Tanıklı söz öbeği bir olay adı olarak çevrildiğinde ve aktarım niteliği bağlamdan anlaşıldığında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yaban hayvanlarıyla sınırlı ölüm olayını doğal bir ad öbeğiyle korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Belirli hayvanlar için doğrudan ölüm sonucu diye yorumlanan dar bir kullanım vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Ölmüş olanın toprağa yerleştirilmesi, ona gömü yeri hazırlanması ve bu yerin adı anlatılır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal ölüm çevresindeki olaylar alanında buluşur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal ölme sonucunu bildirir; komşu dal ölümden sonraki gömme işlemini ve gömü yerini anlatır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Hayvanın ölmesi kullanımın doğrudan karşılığıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Sahibinin gömü yeri yanında bağlanarak ölüme bırakılan binek hayvanına özgü uygulama vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal hayvan ölümüyle ilişkilidir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal yalnızca ölüm okumasıdır; komşu dal belirli bir gömü uygulamasındaki hayvanı ve onun ölüme bırakılmasını anlatır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar incelendi; ölüm ile gömme arasındaki ayrımı ve hayvan ölümüne bağlı özel uygulamayı gösteren iki komşu dışında yararlı anlam örtüşmesi bulunmadı.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه تفسير حشر بعض الحيوان أو الدواب بالموت حيث صرحت المصادر بذلك بلفظ قيل أو رواية.
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس هو المعنى الأصلي للجمع والسوق، ولا يثبت في المصادر كتعريف عام مطلق للحشر.
branches.source_phrase_ar: قيل هو الموت (ayn)؛ حشرها موتها (sihah;tahdhib)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi tekil ve çoğul biçimleri, karada yaşayan küçük hayvanlar için geniş bir eski sınıf adı olarak tanımlar ve küçük kemirgenler, kirpiler ile kertenkele benzeri hayvanları örnekler. Bu yüzden dal modern böcek sınıfına indirgenmemelidir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Kapsam, yalnız böcekleri değil, kaynakların küçük kara hayvanı saydığı farklı türleri içerir; topluluğu sevk etme anlamıyla ilgisizdir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım tekil ve çoğul yalın adları kapsar; kara ile kurulan kalıp aynı sınıfın ortamını belirginleştirir, yeni bir genel kök anlamı oluşturmaz.

concept_map.definition: Karada yaşayan küçük hayvanlar için kullanılan geniş bir eski sınıf adıdır. Küçük kemirgenler, kirpiler ve kertenkele benzerleri örnek verildiğinden, kapsam günümüz Türkçesindeki böcek sınıfından daha geniştir.

facets.statement: Karada yaşayan çeşitli küçük hayvanları tek bir geniş ad altında toplama.
Küçük kemirgenler, kirpiler ve kertenkele benzeri hayvanların bu sınıfa örnek gösterilmesi.
Kara ile kurulan söz öbeğinde sınıfın yerde ve karada yaşayan küçük hayvanlar olarak belirginleşmesi.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar tekil biçimi bu geniş sınıfın bir üyesi, çoğul biçimi ise karada yaşayan küçük hayvanlar topluluğu olarak ortaklaşa açıklar. Verilen örnekler sınıfın modern böcek kavramıyla sınırlı olmadığını gösterir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Modern hayvan sınıflandırması iddiası taşımadan, kaynaklardaki geniş ve eski küçük kara hayvanı kümesini karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Küçüklük, karada yaşama ve birden çok hayvan türünü kapsama özelliklerini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Sınıfın tek bir üyesinden söz edilirken, türü daha fazla daraltmadan kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Tekillik, küçüklük ve karada yaşayan geniş hayvan sınıfına üyeliği korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kara ile kurulan çoğul söz öbeğinin kapsamı açıkça anlatılmak istendiğinde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yaşam ortamını, çoğulluğu ve geniş küçük hayvan sınıfını açıkça korur.
Küçük kara hayvanları düşüncesinin bir bölümünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Küçük kemirgenler, kirpiler ve kertenkele benzerleri gibi böcek olmayan örnekleri dışarıda bırakır.
error_profile.collision: Günümüz hayvan sınıflandırmasındaki daha dar böcek kümesiyle karışır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Çeşitli küçük kara hayvanlarını kapsayan geniş bir sınıf adıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Belirli bir küçük yer hayvanının tekil tür adı ve onun çoğulu söz konusudur.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Komşunun adlandırdığı hayvan, odak dalın geniş küçük kara hayvanları alanına girebilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal üst düzey ve çok türlü bir sınıftır; komşu dal bu alan içindeki belirli bir hayvanı adlandırır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Kemirgenlerden sürüngen benzerlerine kadar genişleyen eski bir küçük hayvan sınıfı vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Karıncalar, tekilleri ve bir yerde ya da yiyecekte bulunmaları özel olarak adlandırılır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Karınca, küçük kara hayvanları alanında düşünülebilecek belirli bir hayvandır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal birçok türü içine alan genel sınıftır; komşu dal yalnızca karıncayı ve ona bağlı biçimleri anlatır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Hayvanın türünü belirlemeden geniş bir küçük kara hayvanı sınıfı kurar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Belirli bir küçük kertenkele türünün özel adı verilir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Küçük kertenkele, odak dalın örneklerle çizilen geniş alanına yakındır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal genel sınıf adı, komşu dal ise tek bir hayvan türünün özel adıdır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar karşılaştırıldı; geniş sınıf ile belirli küçük hayvan adları arasındaki üst kavram-alt tür sınırını en açık gösteren üç komşu seçildi.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الحشرة والحشرات بمعنى صغار دواب الأرض وما يشبهها كاليرابيع والضباب والقنافذ ونحوها، وما جعله بعضهم اسما جامعا.
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس هو فعل جمع الناس أو سوقهم، ولا صفة الدقة في الأذن أو السنان.
branches.source_phrase_ar: حشرات الأرض دوابها الصغار كاليرابيع والضباب وما أشبهها (maqayis)؛ الحشرة ما كان من صغار دواب الأرض مثل اليرابيع والقنافذ والضباب ونحوها (ayn;tahdhib)؛ حشرات الأرض دوابها الصغار واحدتها حشرة (jamhara)؛ الحشرة واحدة الحشرات وهي صغار دواب الأرض (sihah)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, aynı betimleyici biçimleri hayvanlarda sıkı ve toplu beden yapısı, erkeklerde ise iri karın, iri gövde veya şişkin yanlar için kullanır. Bunlar tek bir zorunlu özellik kümesi değil, yoğun ve iri beden görünümü çevresindeki tanıklı değişkelerdir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal küçük kara hayvanı adını ya da incelik-sivrilik niteliğini değil, bedenin sıkı, iri veya kabarık görünümünü anlatır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın betimleyici biçimler sıkı yapı ve iri karın değişkelerini taşır; belirli beden bölümleriyle kurulan kalıp yalnız kendi açık kapsamıyla korunur.

concept_map.definition: İnsan veya hayvan bedeninin sıkı, toplu ve güçlü yapılı olması ya da karın ve yanların iri, dolgun veya kabarık görünmesidir. Kaynaklardaki betimlemeler bağlama göre bu özelliklerden birini öne çıkarır.

facets.statement: Hayvanın veya insanın sıkı, toplu ve güçlü bir beden yapısına sahip olması.
Erkekte karnın ya da bütün gövdenin iri olması.
Özellikle atta yanların dolgun, kabarık veya dışa taşkın görünmesi.
Belirli bir erkek kişi için cinsel organın ve karnın iri olduğunu bildiren beden bölümü kalıbı.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar sıkı ve toplu beden yapısı ile iri karın betimlemelerini ortak alan olarak verir; bazı anlatımlar iri gövdeyi, bazıları şişkin yanları öne çıkarır. Beden bölümlerine bağlı daha dar kullanım da aynı yoğunluk ve irilik görünümüne bağlanır.

concept_gloss.text: sıkı yapılılık ya da iri karınlılık
concept_gloss.applicability: İnsan ve hayvan betimlemelerinde görülen sıkı beden ile iri karın değişkelerini birlikte temsil eder.

error_profile.preserves: Sıkı ve toplu beden yapısını, iri karın değişkeninden ayırarak birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Hayvanın veya insanın beden yapısının toplu, sıkı ve güçlü olduğu bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Toplu görünüm ile sıkı ve güçlü beden yapısını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir erkeğin ayırt edici niteliği olarak karnının büyüklüğü anlatıldığında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: İnsan katılımcısını ve karın iriliği niteliğini doğrudan korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Özellikle bir atın iki yanının dolgun ve dışa taşkın görünümü anlatıldığında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Hayvanın iki yanındaki kabarık ve dolgun görünümü korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: cinsel organı ve karnı iri olmak

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Sıkı beden yapısının yanında iri karın ve kabarık yanlar gibi özel beden görünümleri vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Bir nesnenin dolması ve etin insan ya da hayvan bedeninde birikmesi daha genel biçimde anlatılır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal bedenin dolgun, toplu ve sıkı görünmesini anlatabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal belirli kişi ve hayvan betimlemeleriyle karın ve yanlara uzanır; komşu dal doluluk ve et birikmesini daha genel kurar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Sıkı ve güçlü beden yapısı, karın iriliğinin yanında bağımsız bir değişkendir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Şişkin görünüm, kısa boyla ve çok büyük karınla birlikte betimlenebilir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal iri veya şişkin karın görünümünde örtüşür.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal kısa boy gerektirmez ve hayvanlarda sıkı yapıyı da kapsar; komşu dal şişkinlik ile kısa, iri karınlı görünümü birleştirir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Sıkı hayvan yapısı ve kabarık yanlar gibi karın dışındaki betimlemeleri de içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Yalnızca karnın çok büyük olması niteliğine odaklanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal erkek kişide iri karın betimlemesinde örtüşür.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Karın bağlamında yakın karşılık olabilirler; ancak odak dalın hayvan yapısı ve yanların kabarıklığına uzanan daha geniş bir değişke kümesi vardır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; dolgunluk, şişkin karın ve doğrudan karın iriliğiyle en yakın sınırları kuran üç komşu yayımlandı.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الحشور والحشورة في الدواب والرجال بمعنى تلازز الخلق وشدته، أو عظم البطن، أو انتفاخ الجنبين، وما صرح به تهذيب اللغة من ضخم الذكر والبطن.
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس هو صغر دواب الأرض، ولا دقة الأذن أو السنان، ولا سوق الجماعة.
branches.source_phrase_ar: الحشور من الرجال العظيم الخلق أو البطن (maqayis)؛ الحشور كل ملزز الخلق شديدة (ayn)؛ دابة حشورة إذا كان ملزز الخلق شديده، والعظيم البطن من الرجال حشور (jamhara)؛ الحشور المنتفخ الجنبين، فرس حشور والأنثى حشورة (sihah)؛ حشر فلان في ذكره وفي بطنه إذا كانا ضخمين، والحشور من الدواب كل ملزز الخلق شديده ومن الرجال العظيم البطن (tahdhib)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi kulak, ok tüyü ve mızrak ucunda incelik ile sivriliği açık bir ortak alan halinde verir; hafif ok ve hafif ya da çevik adam kullanımları ise bu alanın kenar değişkeleridir. Bu nedenle dal tek bir evrensel özellik gibi değil, nesneye göre sınırları değişen betimlemeler kümesi olarak tutulmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: İncelik ve sivrilik çekirdektir; hafiflik yalnız tanıklanan ok ve kişi kalıplarında geçerlidir ve bütün dala yayılmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın ad yalnız ince ok tüylerini karşılar; kulak, uç, ok ve kişi okumaları kendi kalıplarına bağlanır ve tek bir yalın anlama karıştırılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Kulak, ok tüyü veya mızrak ucu gibi bir parçanın ince, küçük, sivri ya da inceltilmiş olmasıdır. Okta hafiflik, kişide ise hafiflik veya çeviklik yalnız kendi tanıklı kalıplarında görülen kenar kullanımlardır.

facets.statement: Nesneye göre kulak, ok tüyü veya mızrak ucunun ince, narin ya da sivri olması.
Mızrak ucunu işleyerek inceltme, narinleştirme ve sivriltme.
Belirli ok ve kişi kalıplarında niteliğin hafiflik veya çeviklik olarak gerçekleşmesi.
Kulakların yalnız inceliği değil, yayvanlığı ve keskin uçlu görünümüyle de betimlenmesi.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar kulak, ok tüyü ve mızrak ucu için incelik ve sivriliği ortaklaştırır; işlenmiş uçta bu nitelik yapılan bir işlemin sonucudur. Hafif ok, hafif veya çevik adam ve yayvan-keskin kulak anlatımları nesneye bağlı değişkelerdir.

concept_gloss.text: ince, sivri ya da hafif olma
concept_gloss.applicability: Farklı nesne kalıplarında incelik-sivrilik çekirdeğini ve yalnız tanıklı yerlerdeki hafiflik değişkesini birlikte gösterir.

error_profile.preserves: İncelik, sivrilik ve nesneye bağlı hafiflik değişkelerini ayrı seçenekler olarak korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kulak veya mızrak ucu gibi bir parçanın narin ve belirgin uçlu görünümü anlatıldığında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Parçanın inceliğini ve sivri uçlu oluşunu birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Okun arkasına takılan tüylerin ince ve narin oluşu kastedildiğinde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Ok tüyü katılımcısını ve ona yüklenen incelik niteliğini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Okun ince olmaktan çok hafif oluşunun belirtildiği tanıklı kalıpta kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Ok katılımcısını ve bağlama özgü hafiflik niteliğini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kişiye özgü ayrık kullanımda beden hafifliği veya çeviklik kastedildiğinde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Kişi katılımcısını ve ona özgü hafiflik-çeviklik yorumunu korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Kulak, ok tüyü, mızrak ucu, hafif ok ve çevik kişi gibi birden çok bağlı kullanım vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Yalnızca metal kesici ucun ince oluşu adlandırılır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Mızrak ucu veya benzeri metal uçların inceliğinde iki dal yakınlaşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal mızrak ucunda yakın karşılık verir, fakat kulak, ok tüyü, hafif ok ve kişi kullanımlarına da uzanır; komşu dal ince kesici uçla sınırlıdır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: İncelik ve hafiflik, sivri görünümle birlikte kurucu değişkelerdir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Keskin ucun delici ve etkili olması, kılıçtan dişe kadar daha geniş nesnelere yayılır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Kulak veya silah ucunun sivri ve belirgin olması iki dalda örtüşür.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal narinlik ve inceltilmiş biçime dayanır; komşu dal keskin ucun delici etkisini ve daha geniş uç türlerini öne çıkarır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: İncelik işlenmiş parça biçimi, sivrilik veya nesneye bağlı hafiflik olabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Bedenin zayıflaması ve kesici ağzın kullanımla aşınarak incelmesi anlatılır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dalda da bir nesnenin ya da bedenin inceliği bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal biçimsel narinlik ve sivriltmeyi anlatır; komşu dalda incelik zayıflık veya kullanım sonucu aşınmadır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Ok tüyünün inceliği, okun hafifliği ve mızrak ucunun sivriliği gibi parça nitelikleri vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Ok gövdesinin yontulup kenarlarının düzeltilmesi ve bütün olarak iyi biçimlendirilmesi anlatılır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal ok yapımında inceltme ve düzgün biçim verme alanına dokunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal tüy, uç veya hafiflik niteliğini belirtir; komşu dal okun gövdesinin yontulup düzeltilmiş bütün biçimine odaklanır.
